title_en: The Pilgrimage to the Sacred House of God
body_ar: إن الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينه ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا ومن سيئات أعمالنا، من يهده الله فلا مضل له ومن يضلل فلا هادي له، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له وأشهد أن محمدا عبده ورسوله صلى الله عليه وعلى آله وأصحابه وسلم تسليما كثيرا {يا أيها الناس اتقوا ربكم الذي خلقكم من نفس واحدة وخلق منها زوجها وبث منهما رجالا كثيرا ونساء واتقوا الله الذي تساءلون به والأرحام إن الله كان عليكم رقيبا، يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله وقولوا قولا سديدا يصلح لكم أعمالكم ويغفر لكم ذنوبكم ومن يطع الله ورسوله فقد فاز فوزا عظيما}، أما بعد فإن خير الحديث كتاب الله وخير الهدي هدي محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وشر الأمور محدثاتها وكل بدعة ضلالة...
body_en: Praise belongs to God. We praise Him, we seek His help, and we take refuge in God from the evils of our own selves and from the ill of our deeds. Whomever God guides, none can lead astray; and whomever He leads astray, none can guide. I bear witness that there is no god but God alone, who has no partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger — may God bless him, and his family and his Companions, and grant them abundant peace. {O humankind, be mindful of your Lord, who created you from a single soul and created from it its mate, and from the two of them spread abroad many men and women. Be mindful of God, in whose name you make demands of one another, and of the ties of kinship. Truly God is ever watchful over you. O you who believe, be mindful of God and speak words that hit the mark: He will set your deeds right for you and forgive you your sins. Whoever obeys God and His Messenger has won a great victory.} (Sūrat al-Nisāʾ 4:1; Sūrat al-Aḥzāb 33:70–71). To proceed: the best of speech is the Book of God, and the best guidance is the guidance of Muhammad — may God bless him and grant him peace. The worst of matters are those newly introduced, and every innovation in religion (bidʿah) is misguidance...

flags.note: The standard khutbat al-ḥājah carries three verses — Āl ʿImrān 3:102, al-Nisāʾ 4:1, and al-Aḥzāb 33:70-71. This record has only the second and third; 3:102 is absent. Style guide section 11 applies: the lacuna is left visible and the text has NOT been restored from memory. The source also runs the two surviving verses together inside a single pair of braces with no reference; the English separates them and supplies the references, which is a presentational choice, not a restoration.

flags.note: CRITICAL for display. The record contains only the opening formula of the sermon and its scriptural preamble, and breaks off on an ellipsis at exactly the point where the sermon proper begins. It says nothing whatever about the pilgrimage. A reader arriving at a page titled 'The Pilgrimage to the Sacred House of God' would find the standard sermon opening and no content on hajj at all. Style guide section 9: the full text sits behind /medias/doc/d-b-4.docx and this must never render as a whole sermon.

translator_notes: The opening is the khutbat al-ḥājah, a fixed liturgical formula, and the closing sentence is the standard sermon preamble. Both are recited texts, so the Arabic is the operative text and is retained in full in body_ar per style guide section 4.
The Qur'anic renderings are interpretive and are not a substitute for the Arabic.
'وكل بدعة ضلالة' is part of the fixed preamble, not a ruling the Sheikh formulates here; the English renders it as it stands and adds nothing about its scope or application.
